review_type: Independent read-only source and mathematical completeness review
posted_goal: Existence of a WellFormed AndCountCircuit on the specified Petersen graph with at most6 AND gates, at most2 actual bare-reader gates per variable, and exact maximal-independent-set/one-vertex-extension behavior.
reviewed_points: The15 listed graph edges agree with the posted SimpleGraph.fromRel expression; Boolean edge detection is insensitive to the orientation used to list each edge.

All1024 masks are enumerated to obtain exactly15 maximal independent sets and100 distinct one-vertex extensions. These are exactly the negative and positive inputs quantified by the posted partial specification.
Each selected gate-side summand is either a raw variable or an earlier gate, matching the explicit WellFormed condition and finite-fuel evaluator. No fan-in bound on a free OR side is added.
The side OR equivalences, binary AND equivalences and selected-output OR constraints are correct for empty, overlapping and nested sides; empty outputs and unused gates remain allowed.
Every vertex belongs to a negative maximal independent set, so any output variable would violate a negative row. Omitting output variables is therefore complete for this task.
Any witness with fewer than6 gates can be padded by false gates with both sides empty, preserving old gate values, outputs, well-formedness and all bare-reader counts.
The bare_reader hit is equivalent to left-selection OR right-selection, so a variable on both sides of one gate counts once. Cardinality at most2 is imposed across actual gate identities.

The model imposes no full-edge-function positive requirement. The post-SAT full global-soundness check follows from monotonicity and all maximal-independent negatives; the optional full_edge_function flag is observational.
No unproved symmetry, nonempty-side, disjoint-side, liveness or minimum-size constraint is added.
scope: Source/model review and fixed-circuit controls only. The target run and any external certificate remain separate; no Lean encoding theorem or target result is asserted.
